subject: Clarifications: NIST AI RMF mapping + regression sampling approach for Meridian Health RFP
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@meridianhealth.com>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Geller <tgeller@meridianhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 08 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Meridian RFP - clarification on NIST mapping and regression sampling

Hi Soojin / Marissa,

Thanks for the initial RFP submission. As we review Appendix B we want a bit more detail on two areas before the evaluation panel meets next week:

1) NIST AI RMF mapping: can you provide a compact mapping table that ties Redwood controls to the NIST Core Functions (Govern, Map, Measure, Manage, Protect) and indicate evidence we can review (e.g., policy docs, audit logs, PoC reports)?

2) Regression / sampling approach: for our clinical triage use-case we need to understand how you select samples for regression testing, the minimum sample sizes per release, and the cadence for periodic audits versus trigger-based reviews.

Please include any constraints (PII handling, on-prem vs hosted evidence) and flag what would require a Private deployment. We prefer a short written summary plus a spreadsheet with the sampling logic.

Attachments: Meridian_RFP_AppendixB.pdf (their RFP appendix)

Best,
Elena Torres
Director, AI Procurement
Meridian Health

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 08 Feb 2027 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Meridian RFP - clarification on NIST mapping and regression sampling

Elena — thank you, and great questions. High level response below; attached is a draft deliverable we can iterate on.

Summary (short):
- NIST mapping: we map Redwood operational controls to the NIST functions with direct evidence pointers (policy, SOC2 logs, audit trace). See tab "CoreMapping" in the attached spreadsheet.
- Regression sampling: we propose hybrid sampling — stratified random sampling by intent and clinical severity + targeted sampling on recent rollout cohorts. Baseline minimum: 500 labeled items per major release for high-risk clinical flows; 200 for minor patch releases.
- Evidence scope: hosted API provides telemetry/audit logs, but client-specific PHI-laden artifacts require Private deployment or customer-provided scrubbed extracts.

I'll attach: Redwood_RFP_Response_Draft_v1.pdf and two supporting tables (NIST_Mapping_Table_Candidate.xlsx, Regression_Sample_Proposal.csv). We can walk through these on a short call.

Proposed next steps:
- Technical deep-dive (45 min) this Thursday (your timezone) to review the NIST mapping and sampling spreadsheet
- Deliver a final NIST mapping + sampling matrix by next Monday upon agreement on scope

If that works I'll have Prioym (solutions) and Marissa (governance) join.

Thanks,
So0jin Lee
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Attachments: Redwood_RFP_Response_Draft_v1.pdf; NIST_Mapping_Table_Candidate.xlsx; Regression_Sample_Proposal.csv

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Feb 2027 08:14:00 -08:00
Subject: Internal: proposed language and sample sizes for Meridian

So0jin / Priyom — drafting a few strongly worded, crisp bullets to include in the final:

NIST mapping bullets to include:
- For Measure/Govern: we provide token-level telemetry, evaluation dashboards (per-prompt traceability), and an evidence package that includes sampling indexes and checksumed datasets for audit.
- For Manage/Protect: RBAC + customer KMS support, per-tenant log retention policy (configurable), and optional HSM-backed keying for private deployments.

Sampling / regression bullets:
- Risk-tiered sampling: classify flows into High (clinical triage), Medium (patient messaging) and Low (documentation). For High: 500 labeled instances per major release, 250 per medium release; for Medium: 200/100; Low: 50/20.
- Triggered regression: if a release causes >2% drift on production eval metrics or a customer incident is reported, run an immediate targeted regression (focus on perturbed intents + top error clusters).
- Continuous monitoring: daily seed sampling (n=30) to detect drift signals with automated alerting.

Notes: keep language non-prescriptive on exact metrics (customers often have their own label taxonomies). We'll add a column for "customer-configurable thresholds" in the CSV.

Marissa
Director, Applied ML Assurance
Redwood Inference

From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@meridianhealth.com>

Date: Tue, 09 Feb 2027 11:23:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Meridian RFP - clarification on NIST mapping and regression sampling

Thanks Soojin — that draft is useful. A couple of specific clarifications before we escalate to our security panel:

1) Evidence types: can you confirm the log retention windows (hosted) and what exact fields are included in token-level logs? Our infosec requires retention >= 13 months for telemetry.
2) Third-party evals: do you accept external independent eval reports (e.g., by AuditCo) and can you provide instrumentation to reproduce their sampled runs (seed+model-variant metadata)?

We also need to confirm whether the 500-instance baseline for high-risk flows is considered a minimum for regulatory justification or a recommendation — our compliance team will expect prescriptive language if this goes into the procurement SOW.

Can we meet Thursday 10:30am PT?

Elena

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Meridian RFP - clarification on NIST mapping and regression sampling

Elena / Tom — confirmed for Thursday 10:30am PT. Quick answers in advance so your panel has context: 

1) Hosted retention: default telemetry retention is 13 months for token-level telemetry (configurable up to 36 months under Enterprise plan). Logged fields: timestamp, request id, model_id, model_variant, prompt hash, token stream metadata (no raw PII by default), latency per token, response confidence scores (where available), and policy filter events. For PHI we recommend Private deployment or using our on-prem agent to keep raw payloads customer-controlled.

2) Third-party evals: yes — we accept third-party audit reports. We can provide a reproducibility bundle containing the seed data subset ids, model version, quantization profile, kernel selection metadata, and the execution environment (instance type and runtime version). Repro bundle is provided as an evidence artifact (redacted if needed).

3) 500-instance baseline: position as a pragmatic minimum for high-risk clinical triage in the absence of stronger customer-specific labeling rules. We will state it as a default minimum in the SOW but mark it as configurable by agreement in the contract.

Pre-read: I've uploaded the draft mapping and the regression CSV to our shared folder (link below). I'll bring Priyom and Marissa on the call to walk the sampling logic.

Shared folder: https://redwooddrive.company/meridian/rfp-evidence
HubSpot deal: hubspot:deal_014782-Meridian-Health

See you Thursday — agenda: 1) NIST mapping overview (10 min) 2) sampling logic & cadences (15 min) 3) evidence bundles & deployment options (15 min)

Regards,
So0jin Lee
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
